subtitle: When Granite Could Not Hold the Sky

panels.shot: wide, dusk-lit view of Warangal’s fort walls with Prataparudra II silhouetted on the ramparts, distant campfires of a vast army encircling the city
panels.action: Prataparudra II stands in armour on Warangal’s granite walls, looking out at the encircling Tughlaq siege camps that glow like a ring of fire in the gathering dusk.

dialogue.text: In 1323, as Warangal starved and Delhi closed in, Prataparudra II took a last road north—one that would end by the Narmada and turn Warangal into Sultanpur.

i18n.hi: १३२३ में, जब वारंगल भूखा था और दिल्ली करीब, प्रतापरुद्र द्वितीय उत्तर की आखिरी राह पर निकला—जो नर्मदा पर खत्म हुई और वारंगल को सुल्तानपुर बना गई।

panels.shot: slow push-in from high bird’s-eye over Warangal’s triple fortifications to a medium view of Prataparudra in council
panels.action: Seen from above, Warangal’s stone fortifications encircle its temples and streets; inside a hall, Prataparudra II sits in a simple yet regal posture amid maps and messengers.

dialogue.text: Warangal had stood for generations, its granite walls guarding Kakatiya power. But after Alauddin’s death, Delhi’s new ruler sent his son to break that circle forever.

i18n.hi: पीढ़ियों से वारंगल खड़ा था, उसकी ग्रेनाइट दीवारें काकतीय शक्ति की रखवाली करती थीं। पर अलाउद्दीन की मौत के बाद, दिल्ली के नए शासक ने बेटे को भेजा कि उस घेरे को हमेशा के लिए तोड़ दे।

panels.shot: wide shot of an earlier battlefield landscape, distant Delhi banners withdrawing from Warangal’s walls as defenders watch from the ramparts
panels.action: On the ramparts, Prataparudra II and his men watch as a confused Tughlaq army breaks camp and withdraws, their standards drooping, siege lines in disarray beyond the walls.

dialogue.text: In 1321, Jauna Khan’s first assault failed. Months of disorder, rebels in his rear, and stubborn resistance at Warangal forced the Delhi prince to withdraw in humiliation.

i18n.hi: १३२१ में जौना ख़ाँ का पहला हमला नाकाम रहा। महीनों की उथल-पुथल, पीछे बागी, और वारंगल की अड़ी हुई रक्षा ने दिल्ली के राजकुमार को शर्मसार होकर लौटने पर मजबूर कर दिया।

panels.shot: medium interior shot, Prataparudra in discussion with captains, low-angle to stress gravity
panels.action: Inside a stone hall lit by oil lamps, Prataparudra II leans over a rough map of the Deccan, flanked by armoured captains with anxious faces, as a messenger bows.

dialogue.speaker: prataparudra_ii
dialogue.text: He will return, and stronger. We must be ready in men, grain, and resolve.

i18n.hi: वो लौटेगा, और ज्यादा ताकतवर। हमें मर्द, अन्न और हौसले में तैयार होना होगा।

panels.shot: epic wide shot of a massive Tughlaq host advancing across the Deccan plain towards Telangana, banners rippling
panels.action: A huge Delhi army under Jauna Khan moves across dusty plains, ranks of cavalry and footmen stretching to the horizon, green and black standards of the Tughlaqs rippling in the hot wind.

dialogue.text: In 1323, the prince returned from Delhi as Ghiyath al-Din’s chosen arm. Reinforced, disciplined, he marched south again, determined that Warangal would not slip away twice.

i18n.hi: १३२३ में राजकुमार ग़ियास अल-दीन की चुनी हुई तलवार बनकर लौटा। मज़बूत, अनुशासित, वह फिर दक्षिण चला, ठान लिया कि वारंगल दूसरी बार हाथ से नहीं फिसलेगा।

panels.shot: wide aerial showing Warangal surrounded by multiple rings of Tughlaq camps and watchtowers, roads blocked
panels.action: From above, Warangal appears encircled by concentric rings of Tughlaq camps, trenches, and wooden watchtowers, with the main approach roads cut by patrols and barricades.

dialogue.text: This time Jauna Khan did not rush the walls. He cut the roads, seized granaries, and turned the campaign into a siege of hunger and time.

i18n.hi: इस बार जौना ख़ाँ ने दीवारों पर झपट्टा नहीं मारा। उसने रास्ते काट दिए, कोठारें हथिया लीं, और जंग को भूख और वक्त की घेराबंदी बना दिया।

panels.shot: interior medium shot inside the fort granary, dim light, anxious faces as sacks empty
panels.action: In a dark granary, Prataparudra II stands amid nearly empty grain sacks, listening as an official points to the few remaining stores while soldiers look on, gaunt and tense.

dialogue.text: Weeks turned into months. With the countryside sealed, Warangal’s granaries began to hollow out. A brave garrison could hold the walls, but not refill the barns.

i18n.hi: हफ्ते महीने बन गए। देहात बंद होते ही वारंगल के कोठार खाली होने लगे। शूरवीर फौज दीवारें संभाल सकती थी, मगर भूख की कोठियां नहीं भर सकती थी।

panels.shot: medium shot on the ramparts, defenders weary, Prataparudra looking towards the horizon for allies
panels.action: On the sun-baked ramparts, tired archers rest against the stone as Prataparudra II grips the parapet, searching the empty horizon for any sign of allied banners.

dialogue.text: Beyond the walls, other chiefs watched and waited. No large relief force came. Isolated, Prataparudra faced the Delhi Sultanate with courage—but with fewer choices each day.

i18n.hi: दीवारों के पार, दूसरे सरदार देखते और टोह लेते रहे। कोई बड़ा मददगार लश्कर नहीं आया। कटे हुए वारंगल में प्रतापरुद्र ने हिम्मत से दिल्ली सल्तनत का सामना किया—पर रोज़ उसके चॉइस कम होते गए।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot, Prataparudra in quiet counsel with a close adviser, lamplight and shadows
panels.action: In a quiet chamber, Prataparudra II sits on a low seat, his armour set aside, listening gravely as an elderly counsellor speaks, their faces half-lit by a single oil lamp.

dialogue.text: By the fifth month, famine gnawed at the city. The choice before the Kakatiya ruler was stark: fight until Warangal was ruined, or negotiate and preserve what he could.

i18n.hi: पांचवें महीने तक शहर को अकाल ने काटना शुरू कर दिया। काकतीय राज के सामने सीधी दो राहें थीं: लड़ते रहो जब तक वारंगल बर्बाद हो जाए, या बात करो और जो बच सकता है उसे बचाओ।

panels.shot: solemn wide shot in the fort courtyard where Prataparudra meets Delhi envoys under a canopy
panels.action: In a stone courtyard, Prataparudra II stands straight in ceremonial armour, facing richly robed envoys from Jauna Khan, while soldiers and courtiers watch in tense silence.

dialogue.text: Prataparudra chose surrender. Chronicles say he agreed to yield the fort and accompany the prince north, trusting that honourable terms might spare his people further ruin.

i18n.hi: प्रतापरुद्र ने आत्मसमर्पण चुना। इतिहासी बयान कहते हैं कि उसने किला छोड़ने और राजकुमार के साथ उत्तर जाने पर हामी भरी, भरोसा किया कि इज़्ज़तदार शर्तें उसके लोगों को आगे की बरबादी से बचा सकती हैं।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle shot as the Kakatiya royal standard is lowered from the fort tower
panels.action: From below, we see the Kakatiya banner being lowered slowly from a high tower as Prataparudra II watches, his face composed yet heavy, guards around him standing rigid.

dialogue.speaker: prataparudra_ii
dialogue.text: Better that the city lives, even if my crown does not.

i18n.hi: शहर बचा रहे, भले मेरी ताज न रहे।

panels.shot: wide cityscape shot of Warangal being reorganised, new officials and soldiers in Delhi styles moving through streets
panels.action: Warangal’s streets and gateways fill with Tughlaq officers and soldiers; surveyors measure precincts while local traders watch as new men take charge of old spaces.

dialogue.text: Delhi now ruled Warangal. The city was renamed Sultanpur, and imperial coins were struck here—a stamp of new power pressed onto old stone.

i18n.hi: अब दिल्ली वारंगल की मालकिन थी। शहर का नाम बदलकर सुल्तानपुर पड़ा, और यहीं से शाही सिक्के ढलने लगे—नई ताकत की मुहर पुरानी पत्थर पर।

panels.shot: long shot of a northbound caravan on a riverbank road, Prataparudra under guard, landscape opening
panels.action: A guarded caravan travels along a broad road near fields and tree-lined banks, with Prataparudra II riding in a palanquin or on a horse, flanked by Delhi soldiers.

dialogue.text: Bound by his agreement, Prataparudra left his capital. Northward he went under escort, following the long road toward the Sultan’s domains beyond the Narmada.

i18n.hi: समझौते से बंधा प्रतापरुद्र अपनी राजधानी छोड़ चला। वह उत्तर की तरफ पहरे में चला, लंबी राह पकड़कर नर्मदा पार के सुल्तान के इलाकों की ओर।

panels.shot: medium contemplative shot near the Narmada, calm river behind, Prataparudra seated, guarded yet pensive
panels.action: By the wide Narmada, Prataparudra II sits guarded on a bank, gazing at the flowing water, his expression inward, Delhi soldiers standing at a respectful distance.

dialogue.text: Near the Narmada, the journey ended. Later reports say he took his own life rather than continue deeper into captivity—but the exact moment and manner remain veiled in silence.

i18n.hi: नर्मदा के पास सफर थम गया। बाद की ख़बरें कहती हैं कि उसने कैद में और गहराई तक जाने से बेहतर अपना जीवन खुद समाप्त कर लिया—पर सही घड़ी और तरीका अब भी सन्नाटे में छिपा है।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide shot of Warangal’s temples and fort over years, subtle shifts to show new powers rising
panels.action: Warangal’s fort and temples stand through changing skies, with different groups of armed men and chiefs appearing across the years, hinting at shifting alliances and rulers.

dialogue.text: Warangal did not vanish. In the years after its fall, local nayakas and chiefs adapted to Tughlaq rule, then to its collapse, weaving new coalitions in a changed Deccan.

i18n.hi: वारंगल मिटा नहीं। पतन के बाद के बरसों में, स्थानीय नायक और सरदार तुग़लक हुक्म से, फिर उसके बिखरने से तालमेल बैठाते रहे, बदला हुआ दक्खन में नए मेल-जोल बुनते रहे।

panels.shot: wide shot suggesting a regional gathering of chiefs at a hill-fort, banners of various houses fluttering
panels.action: On a hill-fort terrace, several regional chiefs stand together, their varied banners flying side by side, overlooking a rugged Deccan landscape that stretches to the horizon.

dialogue.text: By the 1330s, as Delhi’s grip weakened, these powers recovered ground. Their movements were not modern nations rising, but a patchwork of regional ambitions and shared interests.

i18n.hi: १३३० के दशक तक, जैसे दिल्ली की पकड़ ढीली हुई, ये ताकतें फिर ज़मीन संभालने लगीं। उनकी चालें कोई आधुनिक राष्ट्र नहीं थीं, बल्कि इलाकाई हसरतों और साझा फ़ायदों की टुकड़ेदार जाल थीं।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of Prataparudra’s weathered eyes from earlier, cross-faded with Warangal’s walls at dusk
panels.action: A close view of Prataparudra II’s intense, weathered eyes dissolves into the image of Warangal’s granite ramparts at dusk, solitary and enduring.

dialogue.text: Prataparudra’s last road shows how even strong rulers can be undone when food, allies, and time fail—and how cities outlive crowns, carrying layered histories in their silent stone.

i18n.hi: प्रतापरुद्र की आखिरी राह दिखाती है कि कैसे मजबूत बादशाह भी टूट जाते हैं जब खाना, साथी और वक्त साथ छोड़ दें—और कैसे शहर ताजों से आगे जीते रहते हैं, अपनी खामोश पत्थरों में परतदार इतिहास सँजोकर।

subtitle_i18n.en: When Granite Could Not Hold the Sky
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब ग्रेनाइट भी आसमान न थाम सका
